draft.title: Simple interest
card: Simple interest is worked out only on the starting amount, called the principal. The interest is not added to the principal each period, so it never earns interest itself.
The formula is I = PrT/100. I is the interest, P is the principal, r is the yearly interest rate as a percentage, and T is the time in years.
The rate is per year, so T must be in years. For 6 months, T = 0.5. Put r in as 6, not 0.06, because the 100 in the formula does that job.
Example: $2000 at 5% per year for 3 years. I = 2000 × 5 × 3/100 = $300. The total amount after 3 years is $2000 + $300 = $2300.
draft.remember: Simple interest is the same every period, because it is always worked out on the principal.

a.q: Mia puts $4000 into an account paying 3% per year simple interest. She leaves it for 2 years. How much interest does she earn?
a.why: I = 4000 × 3 × 2/100 = $240. $4240 is the total balance, but the question asks for the interest alone. $24 000 comes from leaving out the ÷ 100.
a.clue: Use I = PrT/100 with r = 3 and T = 2.

b.q: Sam takes a loan of $5000 at 8% per year simple interest. He repays it after 18 months. How much interest does he pay in total?
b.why: The rate is per year, so 18 months is T = 1.5 years. I = 5000 × 8 × 1.5/100 = $600. Using T = 18 gives $7200, which mixes months with a yearly rate.
b.clue: Change the months into years before using the formula.
